title: Compass Cobblers — patchbook of small fixes & synthesis
content:
Purpose: quick, runnable ideas ("patches") pulled from recent customer threads. This is not a final roadmap — it's a compact lab notebook of things we can ship fast (hours → 2 sprints) to reduce friction and surface wins.

Context and how this doc is structured:
- source window: 2026-05-01 → 2026-06-24 (customer threads, support tickets, field calls)
- intention: triage into three lanes: immediate microfix (<=2w), medium (2–6w), investigation/backlog (>6w)
- each item: symptom, quick mitigation (if any), proposed scope, rough owner/impact, open questions

Topline themes observed (synthesis):
1) Visibility mismatch: customers repeatedly ask for clearer per-route token cost + latency attribution when using model fallback chains and rollouts. They want to see "which model" and "which stage" incurred tokens in traces.
2) KV-cache surprises: prefix caching helps cost but causes unexpected mismatches when prompts are mutated slightly; customers want easy toggles and better debug surfaces.
3) Onboarding friction for private deployments: documentation gaps around KMS keys + service-account bindings during initial VPC bootstrap.
4) Streaming + tools: several customers report truncated tool-call outputs when using streaming mode + function-calling; appears to be borderline race between tool invocation and stream finalization.
5) Cost SLO vs latency SLO tension: enterprise customers want automatic suggestions that balance batching vs latency for specific percentile SLOs (p50/p95) with visible cost delta.

Patchbook (microfix lane <= 2w) — prioritized by expected impact / effort:
A. Route-level token / model attribution toggle (owner: Arjun)
- Symptom: billing/console shows token totals but not broken by model variant in fallback chains.
- Quick mitigation: add a UI toggle to expand request traces into per-hop attribution (show model id, tokens generated, tokens billed) and link to the raw request id.
- Scope: console change + small backend enrichment that tags logs with model_variant. No schema migration.
- Impact: high clarity for customers debugging unexpected token spikes.
- Open Q: need billing team sign-off on exposing token splits in UI (privacy/aggregation concerns).

B. KV-cache debug mode (owner: Diego)
- Symptom: customers see stale completions when they change system instructions mid-session.
- Quick mitigation: server-side "kv-cache-dump" flag that, in non-prod, returns a short hash and TTL of current kv entries for a session (not raw tokens).
- Scope: runtime flag + API surface; doc snippet for SRE.
- Impact: reduces investigation time; educates customers on when cache is used.
- Open Q: ensure dumps don't leak PII; mask identifiers.

C. Streaming+function-call graceful finalizer (owner: Lena)
- Symptom: tool outputs cut off for ~10% of streaming tool calls (reported across customers using medium-length tool outputs).
- Quick mitigation: add a 200ms "stream drain" wait before closing stream when a tool-call completed successfully (configurable per route).
- Scope: runtime tweak + small perf test to measure tail latency impact.
- Impact: small cost to tail latency, large UX win for tool-heavy customers.
- Open Q: should this be default? propose opt-in for 2 weeks then evaluate.

Medium (2–6w) — higher effort but still bounded:
D. Batching advisor in Console (owner: Product: Optimize)
- Symptom: customers manually tune batch sizes and end up with suboptimal p95 latency or cost.
- Proposal: a console panel that shows per-route workload histogram + recommended minibatch sizes and a simulated cost/latency delta for p50/p95.
- Scope: metrics pipeline (sampled histograms), advisor UI, a/b rollout.
- Impact: medium-to-high cost savings and less MTTI for ops teams.
- Open Q: data retention needed for histograms — 7 days minimum?

E. Private deploy KMS quickstart checklist + helper script (owner: Solutions Eng)
- Symptom: initial onboarding stalls on KMS setup and key rotation expectations.
- Proposal: curated checklist plus terraform helper and one-click sample for common cloud providers; include ephemeral test keys for validation.
- Scope: docs + example infra + 1-hour workshop curriculum.
- Impact: reduces time-to-first-requests in Private installs.

Backlog / Investigations (>6w) — collect and monitor:
F. Per-request routing hints API — customers ask for ability to prefer low-cost variant at request time. Needs policy/routing changes and billing semantics.
G. Automated rollout safety net: automatic rollback on quality regressions measured against prompt set. Integration with Optimize evals and rollout system.
H. Embedding drift monitor: alerting when embeddings for a given dataset drift beyond a threshold vs a baseline.

Representative threads & quotes (raw snippets):
- "We saw a 3x token jump when we flipped canary; console shows tokens, not the canary chain — impossible to tell why." — Enterprise platform eng, fintech customer, 6/10
- "Our agents suddenly started giving apparently wrong entity counts after we added short system prompts; we think kv cache is reusing old state." — product manager, ecom startup, 5/29
- "During demo the tool output got cut mid-line; looked like it finished but the last JSON bracket was missing." — solutions architect, 6/14

Quick wins for support playbook (how CS should triage):
1) If cost spike: ask for full trace id; toggle proposed A patch (route-level attribution) will help. Meanwhile ask: model_id, route name, time window.
2) If stale completions: suggest disabling kv-cache for that route and escalate to Diego if reproducible.
3) If streaming truncation: try enabling stream-drain flag in staging for 48h; collect sample request ids to correlate.

Metrics to watch after shipping microfixes:
- Reduction in "billing attribution" tickets per week
- Number of kv-cache investigations opened and time-to-resolution
- Rate of streaming truncate incidents reported
- Time-to-first-request for Private deploy trials (after KMS quickstart)

Risk notes and guardrails:
- Stream-drain small pause could increase p99 for latency-sensitive customers. Start opt-in and publish a clear small-sla note.
- Any cache-dump must redact tokens and PII; coordinate with security.

Next steps (owner + when):
- Arjun: prototype route attribution UI wireframe and share with billing (due 2026-07-08)
- Diego: design kv-cache-dump based on current runtime confidentiality constraints (draft by 2026-07-02)
- Lena: implement streaming drain flag experiment in staging, run 3-day bucketed test (start 2026-07-05)
- Maya (this doc): sync CS + Solutions Eng on 2026-07-01 10:00 PT to triage customer-list for early rollout pilots

Appendix: quick links and artifacts to attach when moving items to GH/Jira
- example traces: attach to CS ticket CS-781
- runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/918 (stream-drain spike test)
- onboarding terraform snippets sketch: repo link to be created (SE-provisioning)

Notes to self: keep this doc short-lived; turn high-priority patches into explicit GH issues and put an owner in the board. Save one sample customer story to include in the release note for each microfix shipped.

End of patchbook (compact).
